s9.title: Einstein Level Plays at SVR F2 | FUNalysis | FRC REEFSCAPE 2025

s13.title: Page with pictures of this robot

auto.text: In a Silicon Valley final a host shows three coral and an algae removal, and later calls it a feeder-station auto.

cycle.text: A full-width ground intake feeds an indexer that orients and stores coral, then feeds it to the end effector. Cameras on AprilTags position the robot to score.
In a Silicon Valley final a host shows it carrying coral while scoring algae in the processor, then scoring the coral and removing another algae.

endgame.text: Spear and fly swatter plates center the deep cage, a gearbox spools string to retract the climber, and friction from the robot's mass keeps the cage from sliding out.

changed.text: Replies that read as the team's say star and flex wheels gave way to printed TPU rollers; a rolling tensioner stopped, in normal use, chain skip found on the practice robot; a planned depth camera was dropped; the carriage motor went from X60 to X44 for weight; and a roller hard stop that was delaminating the side plate was removed for Worlds.

outcome.text: 46-5-0 in official play; ranked 14 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 103.23, Milstein).

facts.text: WCP X2i modules, X60 drive and X44 steer (the team site calls the modules SwerveX), free speed
Square frame side
1 x 1 tubes drop the swerve to reduce ground clearance and lower the center of gravity

solves.text: Pick up coral from any angle and miss fewer pickups

facts.text: The front roller is free to pivot, and polycarbonate wedges center the coral
TPU rollers wrapped in silicone add grip and stay light
Deploys through dual #25 chain at 65.33:1
Front rollers are 1 in and 1.25 in polycarbonate tubes with 2 in and 3 in TPU rollers pressed on (reads as the team's reply)
Slits separate the printed wheel sections, which the post thinks adds compliance (reads as the team's reply)

cost.text: Pressing the TPU segments onto the tubes is very hard, even in 3 in lengths (reads as the team's reply)

functions.name: L1 bar

solves.text: Score L1 by stopping coral from going into the intake

functions.type: carbon fiber blocking bar on the intake

facts.text: Deployed by a Kraken X44 and a polycarbonate sector gear
Hooks on the bar stop the front roller pivoting up, so coral does not bounce out

solves.text: Receive, orient and store coral, and hand it off consistently

facts.text: Front star wheels turn the coral; 2 in flex wheels feed the end effector
A bent polycarbonate tray keeps handoffs consistent
An asymmetric roller layout reduces jams
A beam break triggers automatic ejection when more than one coral is taken in
All shafts geared 2:1

solves.text: Reach L4, and use momentum to score algae in the net

facts.text: Reaches full height in
Two Kraken X60 at 7:1
Two 10 lb constant-force springs counterbalance it and cut current draw
A rolling tensioner keeps the chain from skipping at high acceleration
Tensioner spring rate (reads as the team's reply)
A 1/4 in plate sits less than one link from the sprocket so the chain cannot skip (reads as the team's reply)

functions.name: Pivot
functions.type: chain-driven cantilevered pivot on the carriage

facts.text: Overall reduction 52.08:1, ending in #25 chain with a sliding tensioner
X-contact bearing supports the cantilevered end effector; inside diameter
A three-stage gearbox and the bearing fit in a 7 x 7.5 x 2 space, unit not given (reads as the team's reply)
Only the end effector wires limit rotation; an elastic string shows how far it has turned (reads as the team's reply)

cost.text: Probably a few degrees of backlash on the final stage (reads as the team's reply)

functions.name: End effector

solves.text: Place coral and grab algae in quick succession

functions.type: single-motor coral and algae end effector

facts.text: One Kraken X60, 6.66:1 on the algae side and 5.55:1 on the coral side
3D printed gear and pulley combinations cut weight
Inspired by the Penn State RI3D robot
The team site adds algae pickup from the ground

solves.text: Center the deep cage and lift the robot

facts.text: Weight
Time to lift the robot fully
A torsion spring deploys it after the match starts; a 25:1 MAXPlanetary spools the string
A 1 in round tube and a 0.125 in aluminum gusset touch one cage tube
The team site says dyneema rotates it in and twists the cage
Inspired by the Rusthounds RI3D design

functions.name: Pi Motel

solves.text: Fit four vision computers in a slightly smaller space than three Orange Pis took in 2024 (reads as the team's reply)

functions.type: AprilTag cameras on four Rock 5C computers

facts.text: Cameras on the front swerve modules see the reef AprilTags
Four Rock 5C computers, powered over PCIe by a custom PCB (the team site says Orange Pis)
One camera per computer, three monochrome and one color, running PhotonVision (reads as the team's reply)

functions.name: Underside electronics
functions.type: electronics facing the floor behind removable panels

facts.text: Mounted this way since 2023; mechanisms on top do not block access (reads as the team's reply)

cost.text: Some holes in the 1/16 in panels egged out and broke after a few weeks, so gaff tape held them (reads as the team's reply)

decisions.choice: Printed TPU rollers on polycarbonate tube (reads as the team's reply)
decisions.because: gapless flex wheels were needed for coral arriving across the intake but would be too heavy, and hex shafts bent in impacts
decisions.instead_of: flex wheels on 1/2 in hex shaft
decisions.cost: press fitting the segments is very hard

decisions.choice: TPU roller on top of the intake (reads as the team's reply)
decisions.because: star wheels picked up inconsistently in auto, which the post puts down to intermittent contact

decisions.choice: Rolling chain tensioner (reads as the team's reply)
decisions.because: stretch over a long chain run let it skip and the elevator lost its zero, even with an inline tensioner fully tight
decisions.instead_of: an inline tensioner alone, or heavier #35 chain

decisions.choice: Drop the depth camera (reads as the team's reply)
decisions.because: many teams placed coral accurately with vision alone, and the camera, its computer and a 10 ft cable added weight
decisions.instead_of: an Intel RealSense planned for field tolerance

decisions.choice: Epoxied printed roller hubs (reads as the team's reply)
decisions.because: aluminum tube plugs cracked around the screw holes
decisions.instead_of: aluminum plugs held by two screws
